notes: Access: direct fetch worked throughout, no block encountered (no curl_cffi/proxy needed). The roster URL id=22672 no longer resolves to its own page -- macys.com now redirects/normalizes any legacy id param on /shop/home to id=173142 (same 'Home' department landing); this is an ID renumbering, not a retirement (Rule 3). Extraction scope: macys.com/shop/home/home-decor?id=290059 (23,937 products; itself a mixed roll-up spanning furniture-adjacent and textile lines, so used only as the navigation root, never as a leaf qty), drilled into its 'All Lighting' (Lighting & Lamps, id=39267, 8,546), 'All Mirrors' (id=190359, 1,312), 'All Wall Decor' (id=190360, 614) and 'All Home Accents' (id=190357, 4,391) branches plus the standalone Clocks/Candle Holders/Taper Candles/Flameless Candles nodes. Verification (Rule 1): every one of the ~40 category pages fetched carries an embedded Nuxt page-data JSON with totalResults/resultsPerPage/numberOfPages; resultsPerPage was stable at 60 on every single page (no John Lewis-style A/B drift observed), and ceil(totalResults/60) matched numberOfPages exactly on all ~40 samples. Independently, 4 single-page categories (Track Lighting, Candle Holders, Tapestries, Wall Art>Photography) render a literal 'NN Items' text header in the SSR HTML that matched totalResults exactly in all 4 cases -- no inflation detected for this platform. Raw href/product-ID tile counting was tested and found to UNDERCOUNT here (e.g. Recessed Lighting: 6/6 exact, but Track Lighting 24 of 32, Neon Signs 48 of 49, Candle Holders 12 of 14, Tapestries 5 of 7) -- consistent with the brief's documented tile-counting failure mode (partial SSR/lazy-hydrated grids), so href counts were discarded in favor of totalResults, which passed both checks above. Dedup finding (Rule 0.6): 'Bedside Lamps' (id=341860, totalResults=831) and 'Lamps > Table Lamps' (id=341925, totalResults=831) are the SAME 831-item population -- 29 of 29 sampled product image alt-texts on page 1 were identical between the two URLs. Treated as one listing under two URLs at the same taxonomy tier; kept 'Table Lamps' (the properly nested type node) and dropped the duplicate 'Bedside Lamps' row. Excluded as out of scope: Decorative Pillows & Throws, Window Treatments & Blinds, Wallpaper (settled exclusion), Artificial Flowers/Hanging Plants/Plants/Trees/Wreaths & Garlands (faux-plant exclusion), Diffusers/Oil Diffuser/Reed Diffusers/Soy Candles (home fragrance), 'Candles' node (id=190348, 223 items -- sampled alt text showed the large majority scented, e.g. 'Lavender-Scented', 'Vanilla Scented Soy Wax Candle'; dropped whole node per Rule 1's candle-scent precedent, kept the separately-listed unscented Taper Candles and Flameless Candles nodes instead), Couch Covers & Slipcovers, Ceiling Fans with Lights (fixture+fan exclusion), 'Planters' (id=190624, 'Planter Pots', 938 items -- sampled titles show it is dominated by raised garden beds, greenhouses, garden arbors and multi-tier plant stands, i.e. garden/furniture equipment under an artificial-flowers-plants URL path, not decorative pots; treated as a mixed roll-up and dropped per 'inspect actual titles first'), and 'Kids Room Decor' (id=341248, 140 items -- sampled titles mix picture frames/candlesticks/wall art already captured elsewhere with excluded curtains/textiles; dropped as a cross-cutting mixed room bucket, not a distinct product-type branch). Home Accents caveat: only 5 of its 4,391 products are covered by named sub-nav children (Bowls/Tapestries/Sculptures/Trays/Vases minus excluded Slipcovers = 1,591); the remaining ~2,800 have no identifiable sub-category in the site's own nav or category-tree JSON, so they were left unextracted rather than padding a mixed bucket -- if Macy's exposes finer Home Accents sub-nav in future this should be revisited. Wall Art caveat: its 5 style facets (Canvas Art, Framed Art, Framed Photography & Prints, Shadow Boxes, Wood Wall Art) sum to only 50 of the 263-item parent (19%) -- read as material/style facets, not an exhaustive type split, so the 'Wall Art' node itself (263) was kept as the leaf and its facets were not separately listed. Rule 0 gains: included the full Outdoor Lighting branch (Landscape & Pathway, Outdoor Lanterns, Outdoor Torches, Porch Lights, Post Lights, Solar Lights) and Recessed/Track/Semi-Flush/Flush-Mount lighting that a room-word-averse or depth-limited old-rule worker would likely have stopped short of at 'Ceiling Lights'; included Vanity Mirrors (bathroom-labelled, Rule 0.3/0.4) alongside Large/Round/Wall Mirrors rather than treating 'vanity'/'bathroom' as a blanket exclusion.
